acceptance.dut_violation: post o_scyc!=0 or post o_sstb!=0 in any row with pre.i_reset=1.
env_violation: Master CYC/STB high in a reset row whose previous row was also a reset row (rule 3.20).
A reset pulse that is shorter than rule 3.05 requires.
acceptance.reset_row_events: In a reset row, no acceptance or response is recorded. Rule 3.00: interfaces initialize at that edge.
end_of_row: Discard all live entries, orphans, canceled identities and hypotheses.
Cumulative unresolved records persist for the batch.
acceptance.first_non_reset_row: A slave acceptance in the first non-reset row must match work accepted after the reset (R11). Post of the reset row is judged by the post check above.

clause_matrix.exclusions: DUT o_mack/o_merr inside reset rows are not judged beyond K13 and rule 3.45.

acceptance.write_identity: (WE=1, addr, SEL, data restricted to SEL-enabled byte lanes). SEL=0 compares no data lanes.
multiplicity: Each row with STB high and STALL low is one request, even if its payload equals the previous row's.
A request held through stall is counted once, at the row of acceptance.
Per row: at most one acceptance per master port and one per slave port.
acceptance.undefined_payload: The None check covers only the K2 identity projection of an accepted or held strobed request. That projection is WE, address and SEL, plus SEL-enabled data lanes when WE=1. None in the projection is an env violation on a master port and a DUT violation on a slave port. Read data lanes and SEL-disabled write lanes carry no identity and are never judged (rule 3.60 qualifies payload, but does not make non-identity lanes meaningful).

acceptance: A slave acceptance on port s requires decode(addr)==s.
An unmapped address (decode none) must never be forwarded.

acceptance.consumption: Each slave acceptance consumes exactly one identity-equal candidate. Eligible candidates are a live unforwarded entry of any master (accepted in this or an earlier row of the reset epoch), or a canceled-pool member.
acceptance.consumption_limit: Each candidate is consumed at most once.
acceptance.failure: If no candidate exists in a hypothesis, that hypothesis dies.
acceptance.association_free_projection: For every identity X: count(slave acceptances of X) <= count(master acceptances of X) in the reset epoch.

clause_matrix.acceptance: NOT judged: neither forward order nor side-effect order, within one slave or across slaves. Every scoped_pass report must list K5 as an explicit exclusion. A pass never asserts order preservation. This applies in particular to fault/live_order_swap and new_aba/younger_equal_first.

clause_matrix.source: README 188-196 ('ACK responses won't get crossed'); WB B4 3.1.3.2 ('N ACKs for N transactions', no tag)

acceptance.retirement: A master response in row c retires that master's oldest live entry accepted in a row < c.
acceptance.no_entry: If no such entry exists, the response is invented and the hypothesis dies, with ONE exception. If the response is an ERR (never an ACK) in row c on master m, and row c shows m holding an unaccepted strobed request (pre i_mcyc[m]&i_mstb[m]&o_mstall[m]), the ERR is tagged possible_starvation_err (unknown). Basis: wbxbar.v header 37-39 says a starved master receives a bus error, but gives no phase, timing or precedence. The tagged ERR retires nothing and creates no entry. The held request stays unaccepted, and a later acceptance of it is a normal new entry. The tag does not claim starvation occurred and carries no timing inference. An ACK in the same situation still has no basis: K6 (inferred) invention applies and the hypothesis dies.
acceptance.non_retirable: Canceled and orphan entries are never retirable.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 obs 3.10; 3.1.3.2 ('read data valid with ACK'); README
clause_matrix.status: normative for data validity; inferred for end-to-end preservation
acceptance: A master ACK in row c requires the retired entry to be forwarded and bound to a slave ACK in a row <= c, in the same hypothesis.
A same-row slave-to-master path is allowed (permission 3.30).
For a read, the full 32-bit o_mdata must equal that slave ACK's i_sdata slice.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 perm 3.20, rule 3.45; crossbar article (unmapped -> ERR); wbxbar.v header 32-39 (timeout/starvation)
clause_matrix.status: normative: exclusivity; inferred: decode ERR and slave-ERR propagation; unknown: timeout/starvation conditions and precedence, including ERR on an unaccepted held request (possible_starvation_err, see K6)
acceptance: A master ACK retiring an unmapped entry kills the hypothesis.
A master ACK retiring a slave-ERRed entry kills the hypothesis.
ERR retiring an unmapped or slave-ERRed entry is consistent.

ERR retiring a mapped entry that has no slave ERR is tagged unexplained_mapped_err (unknown). This covers unforwarded entries, entries forwarded but not yet answered, and entries already slave-ACKed. Timeout precedence against a slave ACK is undocumented, so no unconditional no-ERR rule applies.
Neither 'unmapped implies eventual ERR' nor any deadline is asserted. Those would be liveness claims, and no public bound exists.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 3.1.2, rule 3.30; crossbar article abort prose (supplementary)
clause_matrix.status: inferred: no cross-epoch attribution; unknown: survivor set, residual forwarding, latency

acceptance.cyc_drop: In a row where pre i_mcyc[m]=0, every live entry of m changes state at the start of the row. Unforwarded entries become canceled-pool members, tagged with (master, master_epoch, reset_epoch, accept_row). Forwarded entries become orphans.
acceptance.residual_forward: A slave acceptance that consumes a canceled-pool member is tagged post_abort_forward (unknown). This includes the same row as the CYC drop: no public source orders the forward against the abort.
orphan_fate: An orphan stays bound in its slave FIFO.
While pre o_scyc[s]=1, a slave response binds to it positionally and is never routed to a master.
Any master response retiring new work using it kills the hypothesis.
acceptance.persistence: Canceled identities persist until reset. Idle outputs never discard them.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 3.1.3.2 ('waits while STALL'), rules 3.25 and 3.45
acceptance: If pre o_scyc&o_sstb&i_sstall holds in row c with no reset, row c+1 must have either o_scyc=0, or o_sstb=1 with an identical K2 identity projection. The projection is WE, address and SEL, plus SEL-enabled data lanes when WE=1. Read data and SEL-disabled write lanes may change.
o_sstb without o_scyc is a violation.

env_violations: A master changes or withdraws a stalled request while CYC stays high.
A slave asserts ACK and ERR together.
A slave response arrives with an empty FIFO.
A slave response arrives while pre o_scyc[s]=0.
acceptance.result: input_or_scope_invalid. Never reported as a DUT fault.
acceptance.slave_cyc_withdrawal: If pre o_scyc[s]=0, all forwards in slave FIFO s are slave_canceled.

clause_matrix.acceptance: A live entry not retired at trace end, in any surviving hypothesis, gives pending_at_batch_end (unresolved). It is never a liveness failure.
non_obligations: A live entry whose slave forward was slave_canceled can only be ERRed (unknown) or remain pending; a master ACK on it kills the hypothesis.

clause_matrix.source: WB B4 3.1.2 and rule 3.30 (slave role of DUT toward master)
clause_matrix.status: inferred (reading of WB 3.1.2 and rule 3.30 applied to the DUT's slave role toward each master; the rule text constrains response to slave signals while CYC is negated, and this design reads that as forbidding ACK/ERR emission)
acceptance: o_mack/o_merr[m] in row c with pre i_mcyc[m]=0 in both rows c-1 and c is a dut_violation (inferred, K13). No DUT response latency is derived from OPT_DBLBUFFER or any other option name; the one-row allowance follows only from the same-edge observability argument below. A response with CYC low is not an active-cycle retirement, so K6 is not cited as an independent basis for it.
If i_mcyc[m] fell exactly in row c, the response is recorded unresolved same_edge_response_after_abort, because a registered output cannot observe that edge. It is never retired into work.

ownership_algorithm.model: Exact-history nondeterministic reference. The first implementation has no symmetry quotient and no partitioning (both withdrawn per R2/R3). State is a set H of explicit hypotheses for the current reset epoch.
hypothesis_state: Per master: FIFO of live entries.
Each entry carries: identity, accept_row, master_epoch, reset_epoch.
Entry state is one of: unforwarded, forwarded(s,k), slave_acked(data,row), slave_erred(row), slave_canceled.
Canceled pool: a list of distinct member records, not merged even when equal.
Per slave: FIFO of forward records bound to a live entry ref, canceled member ref, or orphan.
ownership_algorithm.counters: master_epoch[m] increments on every CYC 1->0, and reset_epoch increments per reset. The association-free projection counters are also arbitrary-precision in the checker: per-identity master and slave counts, per-slave forwards and responses, and per-master acceptances and responses in the current CYC. None of them is ever pruned or truncated when hypothesis resources are exhausted, so the projections stay exact and sound. If a bounded implementation is used and any counter would overflow, that counter's projection becomes unresolved_on_counter_limit(row) for the rest of the reset epoch. It never wraps or saturates into a verdict.
row_order: 0 Reset row: apply K1 and stop processing the row.
1 CYC drop: for each m with pre i_mcyc[m]=0, apply K9 transitions. If 1->0, increment master_epoch[m].
2 Master acceptances: append new live entries (accept_row=c).
3 Slave CYC: for each s with pre o_scyc[s]=0, mark all FIFO-s forwards slave_canceled and empty the FIFO.
4 Slave responses: apply K11 env checks, then bind each to its FIFO-s head among forwards from rows < c.
5 Slave acceptances: branch over every identity-equal candidate (live unforwarded from rows <= c, or canceled member), and append to FIFO s.
6 Master responses: apply K13, then K6/K7/K8 retirement against entries from rows < c, using slave responses from rows <= c.
7 Association-free checks: K3, K10 and env hold, independent of H.
same_edge_dependencies: Slave response row c can retire only forwards from rows < c.
A forward in row c may consume a master acceptance from row c. This is permissive and adds branches only.
A master response in row c may use a slave response from row c, but never a master acceptance from row c.
A forward in the same row as a CYC drop is tagged post_abort_forward.

verdict_semantics.trace_membership: Exists a surviving hypothesis. If H becomes empty, the result is dut_violation. Cite the dying row, the per-branch witnesses and every inferred clause that was used.
verdict_semantics.clause_level: With H nonempty, a judged clause is pass only if no surviving hypothesis carries an unknown tag (post_abort_forward, unexplained_mapped_err, same_edge_response_after_abort) and none has pending work. Otherwise it is unresolved(clause), listing the alternatives and their downstream consequences.
verdict_semantics.aggregate_precedence: Time-bounded. Let e be the first row with an env violation. (1) A DUT violation whose complete evidence lies in rows < e stays dut_violation; a later invalid input cannot erase it. (2) A DUT violation evidenced in row e itself, as a same-edge mixed fault, is reported as mixed_same_edge(dut_candidate, env) with the explicit note that no public ordering exists. It is unresolved for the DUT, unless the DUT check depends only on pins and on inputs from rows < e. (3) Every judgment needing rows >= e is input_or_scope_invalid. A clause whose evidence lies wholly before e may still be reported as prefix_scoped_pass, bounded to rows < e. (4) Trace aggregate: dut_violation if (1) applies, else input_or_scope_invalid if e exists, else violation > unresolved > pass. Both the env record and any prefix verdict are always listed.
verdict_semantics.ownership: unique-by-elimination only if all survivors agree; otherwise indistinguishable(k). Never a hidden-state claim.
non_circularity: A hypothesis is removed only when a specific observed pin value contradicts an independently cited clause applied to that branch's bindings.
A pass is therefore 'not refuted by the reference', a membership statement. It is not universal evidence that the DUT satisfies the clause on other traces, and not proof of internal ownership.
Universality is evaluated only over the unknown-tag and pending dimensions, never over clauses used for filtering.

resource_limits.constants: MAX_HYP=4096, MAX_LIVE_PER_MASTER=64, MAX_CANCELED_POOL=256. Declared, test-lowerable, never silently changed.
resource_limits.on_exhaustion: No pruning and no branch selection. For the remainder of the current reset epoch, record unresolved_on_limit(row, sizes) and suspend all association-dependent judgments for all masters: K4 per-candidate consumption, K6, K7, K8 attribution, K9 tags and K12. Violations recorded before the exhaustion row stay final. Mandatory metric for each run and each clause: suspended_rows, total_rows, the suspended fraction, and the exhaustion rows and sizes. A clause suspended in any row may never be reported scoped_pass; the best it can be is unresolved(suspended). The report also states the effective checked scope in rows.
still_valid_after_exhaustion: K4 association-free count projection per identity

Per-master ACKs in current CYC <= acceptances in current CYC. ERRs in the same CYC are counted against acceptances, except an ERR that meets the K6 possible_starvation_err condition. Such an ERR is counted separately and tagged unknown.
resource_limits.resume: Only at reset. This removes the R4 contradiction: there is no mid-epoch closure.

label_change_log_before_replay: unresolved/identical_heads -> scoped_pass. The m1-first branch dies by K7 at the m0 ACK (cycle 12); clauses hold.
negative/early_unexplained_error -> unresolved. The ERR on mapped unforwarded work is K8-unknown and no deadline exists.
fault/live_order_swap -> scoped_pass. Only forward order differs, and K5 is not judged.
new_aba/younger_equal_first -> scoped_pass. Same-address forward order is not judged and data retire consistently via the A2-first binding.
negative/stale_after_reset keeps dut_violation, but its basis is now K13 plus K6 invention, not epoch inference.

formal_obligations.status: Targets only. Nothing implemented or proved. No certificate is supplied.
quantifier_note: Trace membership is an existential property: there exists a history explaining the trace. Standard safety tools check universal properties over all paths and free inputs. A free ghost association variable therefore asserts over ALL associations, and a failing arbitrary association is not a DUT failure.
Membership is expressible only via a determinized monitor. That monitor is the H set, with explicit finite bounds as assumptions, and the claim is bounded.
No harness may assign associations from internal state or assumed order, and the property under proof must not appear in assume form.

items.prop: For all rows: slave acceptance on s implies decode(addr)==s, and an unmapped address is never forwarded.
For a free constant identity X: cnt_s(X) <= cnt_m(X) since reset.
requirements: If induction fails, report BMC depth only.
items.false_control: Trace/RTL mutation control, not a property edit. Use a reachable stimulus in which X is accepted once and the mutated DUT forwards X twice (the fault/duplicate_consumed_identity pattern). It must fail, and a cover must reach the second forward. A property-harness sanity mutation, such as the trivial strict-< form, may be logged only as a harness check; it is never evidence of transaction sensitivity.

items.prop: A synthesizable bounded determinization of the reference never reaches an empty H.
assumptions: Explicit bounds on outstanding entries, canceled-pool size and epoch width, each disclosed
items.false_control: DUT/trace mutation: retirement data swapped across cross-slave reads (the cross_slave/wrong_retirement_data pattern) must drive the unmutated monitor to empty H, on a reachable cover with both forwards and both slave ACKs. A monitor-mutation run is labeled harness-only.

items.prop: No master response is retired using a slave response bound to a forward whose epoch tuple predates the entry's.
items.notes: Monotone counters; repeated-abort cover required. Embedded in the F3 monitor, not a free ghost tag.

items.prop: ACK never retires an unmapped or slave-ERRed entry, evaluated inside the monitor.
items.notes: Mapped ERR is unconstrained, and no deadline is asserted.

characterization_only.question: Restart-safe noninterference: after an abort, does no old-identity forward follow any new acceptance or repeated abort?
characterization_only.use: Certificate required before canceled identities may be discarded.

characterization_only.question: Timeout and starvation ERR conditions and their precedence.

formal_obligations.vacuity: Every assert needs a reached cover; otherwise its evidence is void.
